name: Orbanism
summary: Orbanism is the governing approach of Viktor Orbán and Fidesz in Hungary since 2010. It rejects liberal democracy for an 'illiberal', Christian-national state in which the majority and the national community outrank individual rights and independent checks. It pairs strong sovereignty and anti-migration politics with pronatalist family policy, a work-based alternative to welfare, a flat tax, and an interventionist, nationalist economy.
scope: The Fidesz governments of Viktor Orbán from 2010 as an ideology of governance: the 2014 'illiberal state' speech, the 2019 'Christian liberties' formulation, the 2011 Fundamental Law and the record of policy. Critics dispute whether it is a coherent ideology rather than a method of expanding power; answers follow stated positions and documented policy, with low confidence where the sources are silent.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Hungary keeps a tax-funded public health system and the Fundamental Law lists illness assistance as a state duty; Orbanism has not attacked it, though the answer is inferred rather than a defining stance.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred: the work-based state wants work to pay more than aid, so adherents lean toward higher wage floors, but no source states the position.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Orbanism mixes market elements with nationalisation, sector taxes and state monopolies, so adherents reject a general claim that markets beat government.

public-ownership.rationale: The ideology's record includes nationalising utilities and building state monopolies, though Orbanism favours national (often friendly private) ownership over a doctrinal public sector.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The signature tax policy is a low flat income tax (16% from 2012), which is the opposite of heavier taxes on the wealthy.

unions-good.rationale: The "work-based state" stresses duty to work and the government sidelined independent civil-society actors; unions are not a favoured partner, but explicit statements are scarce.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Fundamental Law protects property, but Orbanist governments readily override it for national-interest nationalisations, so adherents give only mild support.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The record documented in the Orbanism article includes market regulation, nationalisation and state monopolies, so adherents accept tighter regulation of firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: Adherents split in rhetoric: welfare-skeptic "work not welfare" language coexists with large family-benefit spending, so neither side is clear.

worker-ownership.rationale: Nothing in Orbanism supports collective worker ownership; its ownership aim is a national bourgeoisie of private owners, so this is inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Orbanist governments stress security against external threats and have expanded state oversight, but explicit counterterror-surveillance doctrine is thin.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Orbanism is socially conservative with strict drug laws in practice; no primary statement was found, so the answer is inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The Fundamental Law bars speech violating the dignity of the Hungarian nation and communities, yet the government attacks speech limits from liberals; adherents are split.

strong-leader.rationale: Orbán's project concentrates power in the government to avoid gridlock and defends it as serving the national will, which is central to the model.

state-harmful.rationale: Orbanism wants a strong state serving the nation; the Fundamental Law says democracy is only possible where the state serves its citizens.

limit-guns.rationale: Hungary has strict gun laws that Orbanism has not challenged and no stated position exists, so this is genuinely unclear.

empower-police-military.rationale: The ideology has a militaristic, security-first emphasis and the Fidesz governments built up the border force and army.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Social conservatism and Christian values imply opposition, but no direct statement was found.

decide-locally.rationale: Inferred from Orbanism's aim to maximise the power of the government and diminish civil society; the sources do not show local competences being cut, and Wikipedia notes social responsibilities were delegated to local governments.

rehabilitation.rationale: A law-and-order posture implies a punitive emphasis, but the ideology has no explicit penal theory.

traditional-family.rationale: Article L protects the family as the basis of the nation's survival and defines marriage as man and woman.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Fundamental Law defines marriage as between a man and a woman and Orbán's governments restricted same-sex adoption and LGBT content.

abortion-legal.rationale: Pronatalism and Christian values imply opposition to broad legality, but no source states an abortion policy, so this is inferred and moderate.

more-religion-public.rationale: Orbán calls Hungary a Christian state and says democracy could not exist without Christianity, though the stress is cultural-civilisational rather than devotional.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Orbán's 2022 speech and the exclusive view of the nation point away from race-conscious corrective policy; the topic is marginal in Hungary.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Article L defines marriage as man and woman, and in 2020 Orbán's government ended legal recognition of transgender people, which rejects a social-construct view of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The National Avowal and Orbanism centre on Hungarian identity, history and Christian roots.

gradual-change.rationale: Orbán describes a "revolutionary government" that rebuilt constitutional order after 2010, which is not gradualism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Orbán built a border fence in 2015, rejects EU quotas and calls migration an existential threat.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Orbán wants to reduce the Commission's role and stresses sovereignty against external interference.

free-trade.rationale: Orbanism favours economic nationalism and state intervention, though Hungary is trade-dependent and exporting, so only -1.

nation-first.rationale: National sovereignty and the national interest, as the government defines it, are central.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The foreign policy is sovereigntist and non-interventionist toward others, treating human-rights interventionism as liberal overreach.

open-borders.rationale: Orbán calls migration an outside threat Hungary has defended itself against and ordered the 2015 border barrier, so open borders contradict the programme.

limit-growth.rationale: The ideology prizes work and growth; its record is pro-industry and sceptical of EU climate rules.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Orbán's governments resist costly EU climate mandates while backing nuclear power, so adherents do not accept the drastic-action claim.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No doctrinal position; Orbanism looks to demographics and culture rather than technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Orbán signed the Paks II nuclear deal with Rosatom, showing government commitment to expanding nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Orbán's "revolution" was electoral and constitutional; the ideology defends order against street politics, though it uses revolutionary rhetoric.

experts-over-public.rationale: Orbanism elevates the popular majority's will as the government defines it, over technocratic and expert bodies, though it controls academia too.

central-planning.rationale: Interventionist but market-based; "unorthodox" economy is not planned.

socialized-markets.rationale: The state-owned/worker-owned market framing is not Orbanist; its target is a national private middle class.

land-value-tax.rationale: It favours a flat income tax; no support for a land tax is documented.

tax-inheritance.rationale: A low-tax, family-centred model suggests opposition to heavy inheritance taxes; inferred from the flat-tax approach, not stated.

basic-income.rationale: Orbán explicitly opposed universal basic income, favouring job-focused policy.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The government favours protecting national firms, but mostly via ownership screening and sector taxes within EU rules.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The government uses public funds to build a national middle class and champion firms.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The aim of a national middle class implies broad property, but oligarch concentration contradicts it; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Implied by the work-based market order Orbanism builds; abolishing money and wages is never discussed in the sources.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The government kept the central bank, asserting control of it over the ECB rather than abolition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: No evidence of state-recognised tripartite wage setting as doctrine.

one-party-rule.rationale: Orbanism operates through multiparty elections it dominates; it does not claim single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Fundamental Law honours the historic constitution and Holy Crown, but there is no monarchist programme; split.

democracy-best.rationale: Orbán claims democracy but redefines it as majority-based and Christian, rejecting liberal democracy; "even when voters choose badly" is not a position he endorses.

direct-votes.rationale: Orbán used referendums (2016, 2022) and national consultations, but not as a general principle.

workers-councils.rationale: Implied by Orbanism's strong parliamentary nation-state with a two-thirds majority; council government is never discussed in the sources.

right-to-secede.rationale: The Fundamental Law speaks of one Hungarian nation; the state defends sovereignty, and Hungarians in neighbouring states are not offered secession either.

natural-rulers.rationale: The government defines the national interest alone, but no doctrine of natural rulers appears.

political-violence-never.rationale: Orbanism is not violence-oriented; neutrality, but the "revolutionary" language leaves room, so a mild agreement.

war-builds-character.rationale: Militaristic tone is documented, but not a glorification of war.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Fundamental Law invokes Christian Europe, and Orbán calls the state Christian.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Christian values shape the constitution without making scripture law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The model rests on a strong state; the Fundamental Law makes defence a civic duty and critics describe Orbanism as maximising state power, leaving no room for privatised courts or armies.

military-superiority.rationale: The militaristic stance serves Hungarian interests but Hungary is a small state with no rivalry aim.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Orbán's 2022 remarks and the "one Hungarian nation" in Article D imply ethnic-cultural nationhood, though Hungary has recognised nationalities.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Implied by Orbanism's view of the nation and Christian civilisation as the actors of history; class conflict is not discussed in the sources.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Orbán rejects egalitarian economics and 'European socialism'.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: No positions on this; implied by an ethnic-national outlook that rejects group-rights claims.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Hungary had no colonies and the ideology rejects Western guilt politics; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Orbán's Christian Europe is cultural, while politically he wants to cut back the Commission and keep power with national governments, so political union of a civilization is inferred to be opposed.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The nation-first morality puts service to the community above private choices.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Orbán says individual freedoms can never encroach on the interests of the community.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: None of the sources link Orbanism to an environmental philosophy; adherents have no distinct view, so neutral.

limit-population.rationale: Article L encourages couples to have children and Orbán wants EU money spent on families having more children, the opposite of limiting population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The ideology builds on value-creating work and an industry and export economy; it blames liberalism, not industrial society, for decline.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred: a project built on preserving tradition and a Christian order ranks stability above institutional disruption, but technology is not addressed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from the social conservatism and Christian values of the project; no source addresses transhumanism.

algorithmic-government.rationale: No documented stance; the state-personal leadership model implies rejection.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from a security-first, state-power-maximising approach, which would resist citizens holding state-proof communications; not directly sourced.

restore-past-order.rationale: The National Avowal restores the historical constitution and Christian national order, but the project also presents itself as modern.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Orbán describes his government as pragmatic and critics cite shifting positions.

direct-action.rationale: Orbanism works through parliament and electoral supermajorities.

means-match-ends.rationale: Orbanism does not frame method-end consistency as a principle; adherents are indifferent, so neutral.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Clearly implied: a modernising, work-based capitalist state has no place for a primitivist ideal.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Clearly implied by an economy resting on value-creating work and freedom of enterprise (Article M).

distribute-by-need.rationale: The work-based state rewards work and contribution; need-based distribution is the opposite of its welfare-skeptic workfare.

production-for-use.rationale: The Fundamental Law bases the economy on value-creating work and freedom of enterprise.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Fundamental Law bases the economy on enterprise and Orbanism defends a national owner class, so it rejects the exploitation theory of profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Orbanism treats the nation, not a class, as the political subject and is anti-communist; inferred from its nationalism.

collective-farming.rationale: Implied by its aim of a national property-owning middle class; no collectivist agriculture appears in the sources.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Orbanism is a nationalist capitalist order and does not use a Leninist theory of imperialism; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Implied by the strong, tax-funded state with large family benefits; the libertarian view of tax as theft is not discussed in the sources.

harm-principle.rationale: The ideology limits individual freedom for community and Christian values.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Article D recognises collective rights of Hungarian communities abroad, and Orbán places the community above the individual.

conscription.rationale: Article XXXI allows compulsory service in a national crisis.

exit-over-voice.rationale: It stresses the national community and the vote of the majority.

state-as-business.rationale: Orbanism sees the state as a national and moral community, not a business; though 'competitiveness' language appears in 2014.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social rights exist in the Fundamental Law while the state emphasises work duty; split.

media-academia-power.rationale: Orbán's circle treats liberal media, academia and NGOs as an illegitimate elite power, and created a parallel system in culture and academia.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Orbán referred to race in 2022 but clarified it was cultural, so he does not endorse genetic claims.

organic-representation.rationale: Parties and parliament remain the channel; the National Avowal names no corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: The state is dominant but not total in the fascist sense; the economy retains private enterprise.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rhetoric of rebuilding Hungary after liberal "decadence" appears, but is not a rebirth ideology proper.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Hungarian goals are kinship with communities abroad, not conquest.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority is grounded in a constitution and elections, even if critics describe personalised rule; no feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: The work-based state compels work as a condition of aid but through municipal public work schemes, not legal bondage to a lord.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The ideology reads liberal academia as power-driven, but claims the truth for itself.

universal-morality.rationale: Orbanism emphasises civilisational particularity and Christian values.

single-common-good.rationale: The government alone defines the national interest, and says individual interests yield to the community.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Orbán is strongly pro-Israel in practice, although the position is not doctrinal.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Article D and the status law and fast-track citizenship for co-ethnics express diaspora membership.

revive-national-language.rationale: The question does not arise as Hungarian is the everyday language; adherents have no stake, so neutral.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The model treats the state and national owners, not workers, as economic leaders and sidelines civil-society actors (s4); inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred: the movement centralises education under state direction and a parallel cultural system, not parental market choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Orbán's record is mixed, blending deficit-conscious rhetoric and unorthodox spending.

economic-freedom.rationale: The model deliberately has liberty dependent on Christian liberties and state, not economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Orbanism uses law and state power to enforce Christian and national values rather than relying on rulers' example; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Article D speaks of one Hungarian nation, and sovereignty against outside interference is the ideology's core.

force-without-un.rationale: Sources show a sovereigntist anti-interventionist tone but no stated view on unauthorised force; neutral.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Orbán says democracy cannot exist without Christianity and calls the state Christian, so faith and tradition are not subordinated to reason alone.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare is for Hungarian families and workers, and migration is treated as a threat.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The work-based state is the defining social policy; Boell describes the public work scheme as central to the 'work-based' alternative to welfare.

class-collaboration.rationale: The programme speaks of a national community and nation over class; its outlook is cooperative rather than class conflict, though not formally corporatist.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The National Avowal stresses inherited culture, the historical constitution and Hungarian heritage, which adherents would not sacrifice.

dominated-front.rationale: Orbán's anti-Western-liberal and pro-Russia stance suggests sympathy, but the sources show no formal anti-Western front; neutral.

workers-nation.rationale: Nation-first orientation implies national workers, but not doctrine.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The family policy relies on gender-specific roles, but equal rights are in Article XV.

ban-interest.rationale: The economy rests on enterprise and the state defends the flat tax and market regulation; there is no ban on lending at interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Article XV forbids discrimination on grounds including race; Orbán's 2022 remarks concerned peoples, not segregation law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Orbanism sees the state as embodying the nation and serving citizens (s1), not as a class instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from close energy ties with Russia and the pragmatic energy stance; no direct source on domestic fossil expansion.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Orbán rejects multiculturalism and wants migrants kept out rather than integrated, but where admitted, adaptation is expected.

elite-replacement.rationale: Wikipedia states that in May 2022 Orbán promoted the Great Replacement conspiracy theory in a speech, an explicit endorsement rather than a hedged one.

proportional-representation.rationale: Boell describes electoral changes favouring governing parties; adherents prefer majoritarian outcomes that give clear mandates.

national-mission.rationale: The aim is protecting Hungarian identity, not exporting a model, although Orbán offers an illiberal example to others.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from the traditional family model of Article L and the government's anti-gender policies; the opened sources do not discuss structural patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The movement is populist and presents Brussels and liberal elites as corrupt, though its own record is criticised.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The Fundamental Law is pronatalist and has no eugenic provisions; the sources document no such policy.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The government resists accountability for past regimes less directly; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Orbanism maximises state power over economy, culture and society, so a minimal state is rejected.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Orbán's 2022 line concerned mixing among peoples but he said his meaning was cultural.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Article XV states equality before the law, yet the nation is exclusive.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The Marxist debate has no counterpart in Orbanism; indifferent, so neutral.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from Orbán's close relations with Israel; no source states the view on settler colonialism.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Article XV gives equality before the law, but religion-based civil law is not an issue in the sources; weak inference.

restrict-conversion.rationale: No source mentions restricting conversion; inferred from a constitutional framework that guarantees religious freedom while favouring Christianity.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle slaughter is not an Orbanist concern; it follows from a Christian, market-based economy that the ban would be opposed (inferred).

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Orbán says Hungary is an illiberal Christian state, so religious instruction in schools is compatible, not opposed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist question without an Orbanist counterpart, so neutral.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The National Avowal anchors legitimacy in citizens and elections.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred from the economic-nationalist, competitiveness-focused approach; no direct statement.

population-transfer.rationale: No source describes expulsion policy; Orbán's targets are migrants, not resident minorities, so the answer is an inference.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Orbanism builds on state power, a conscript duty and a militaristic stance, so it rejects the absolute non-aggression principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Orbán's 2014 language stresses competitiveness among states.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The sources do not address banning parties; adherents are unspecified, so neutral.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican concept is not Orbanist; its vision subordinates individual freedom to the community, so inferred disagreement.

separated-powers.rationale: Boell finds systematic removal of checks and the Fundamental Law is used for majority rule.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist concept foreign to a nationalist, anti-communist movement; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The welfare approach prioritises working families, not the poor; Boell describes a work-based state over welfare.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: No source addresses council housing; neutral.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from the work-based state and sidelining of civil-society and union actors; no direct source.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Orbanism is pronatalist and welfare-focused on families, rejecting any Malthusian view of poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Orbán opposes mixing of peoples from different civilisations and ethnic diversity in Hungary, including the 2022 'mixed race' speech.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The ideology relies on elections and party leadership; lottery is a radical alternative with no support.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Boell describes a 'permanent crisis' framing used to justify exceptional rule; adherents back extraordinary powers.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from the state-interventionist economy and market regulation; no specific source on food price caps.

party-controls-media.rationale: The media system is concentrated in aligned hands, but not formally party-owned.

party-commands-army.rationale: Fundamental Law makes defence a state duty; Orbanism is not a Leninist party-army model.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the restrictive migration stance and tightened asylum rules, though the sources give no residency figure.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: A populist Marxist demand foreign to Orbanism; implied opposition.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Fidesz is hierarchical but the sources give no doctrine on binding party decisions; neutral.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Orbán wants to reduce the Commission's role and keep national governments in charge, opposing more pooling.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Fundamental Law is parliamentary, with a ministerial government; Orbán is a prime-minister-centred figure, so presidential command is not his model.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The question concerns church governance, which Orbanism leaves to the churches; neutral.

clerical-rule.rationale: Orbán calls his state Christian but the leadership is political and secular; clerical supremacy is not part of it.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The nation-first ideology is incompatible with revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The government funds cultural direction, but no formal censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Orbán has served consecutive terms with no limit, but it is not formal doctrine.

recall-officials.rationale: Not part of the programme, which prefers strong stable mandates; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Hungary remains in NATO and Orbán approved Finland's and Sweden's accession, so adherents do not seek ending alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: A radical measure that the property-friendly Orbanism does not propose.

people-in-arms.rationale: Article XXXI maintains a volunteer reserve with conscription in crisis, but not replacing the professional army; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The national-romantic, traditionalist self-image suggests sympathy, but no source states it.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Article D says there is one Hungarian nation that belongs together, though pursued through ties and citizenship, not borders.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist anti-elite rhetoric suggests agreement, though the sources do not mention educated people specifically.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Orbán says Western liberal civilisation fails and Christian culture is superior.

death-penalty.rationale: Orbán has mused about reintroduction, but it has not been policy.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The government restricted LGBT-inclusive education, so adherents would oppose gender-equality curricula.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Orbanism is Christian-cultural but no source shows a creationist education policy; slightly negative.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from Christian social conservatism and child-protection concerns.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Co-ethnics got simplified naturalisation; a nation of descent is central.

minority-language-support.rationale: Article D wants it abroad for Hungarians, while the Avowal recognises domestic nationalities.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; a Christian-majority state rhetoric yet no sourced stance on minority exemptions.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: No source gives an Orbanist stance on this issue; neutral.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Economic nationalism (national middle class) suggests partial support, but no property transformation; split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Fidesz wrote its Fundamental Law in parliament by supermajority.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: In 2014 Orbán held up Singapore, China and Russia as models and the work-based state subordinates liberal freedoms to competitiveness.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Orbán wants EU money directed to families rather than migration, a nationalist priority over global aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Hungary has no nuclear weapons debate in the sources; neutral.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Hungary elects its president by parliament and the Fundamental Law kept this; no push for direct election in the sources.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Orbán's government passed a central bank law presented as more independence from the ECB, and Orbán is accused of reducing the independence of Hungary's central bank from his government.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Article D and the 'one nation' idea suggest reluctance over territory, but the sources show no Hungarian peace-for-land scenario; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Boell shows collective national interest overriding individual rights, and nationalisations override property when the government finds it necessary.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Marxist debate with no Orbanist counterpart; neutral.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from resistance to EU regulation; no source states it.

collective-defense.rationale: Hungary remains in NATO and Orbán approved allies' accessions, so mutual defence is accepted in principle.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Orbán opposes Ukraine's NATO and EU accession and kept ties with Russia, but the sources give no view on annexed territories.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The government funds and strengthens churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Hungary's president is a ceremonial office elected by parliament; the sources give no doctrine on this.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the strong sovereignty and unity of the state, but no source on secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: No source addresses autonomy within a larger state; neutral.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Fundamental Law makes the head of state an elected office; no divine ruler concept appears.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Orbán's government introduced a 16% flat personal income tax in 2012; it is a defining economic measure.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred from the stress on nation, culture and inherited identity over environment-shaped character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The government claims law-making but within its Fundamental Law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not a priority in the sources; inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Boell describes concentration of power in the governing party, not a balanced mixed constitution.

leader-cult.rationale: Critics see personalised power but the sources do not show formal leader-cult practice; neutral.

equal-parenting.rationale: Article XVI treats parents' duties but the sources give no stance on custody presumptions; neutral.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist idea with no Orbanist content; implied disagreement.

land-redistribution.rationale: Orbanism aims to broaden national property but no land seizure appears in the sources.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from the hostility to migration and refugees; the context of expelled refugees is not discussed.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Article D and status law; there is a non-territorial support instead of claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Fundamental Law recognises freedom of religion; there is no such legal punishment.

women-must-cover.rationale: Article XV protects equal rights for women and men; there is no dress mandate in the sources.

common-currency.rationale: Hungary keeps the forint and Orbán's government asserts sovereignty over monetary stance, opposing deeper EU integration.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The sources show a Hungarian-national, not pan-Finno-Ugric, focus; neutral.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Article D backs Hungarian communities abroad having collective rights, but a state-less autonomy model is not stated; split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Orbán stresses culture, Christianity and national identity as the drivers of politics, rejecting historical materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Article M tells the state to act against abuse of dominant position, but the government favours national champions; split.

no-bailouts.rationale: Orbanist governments use public funds to support national firms; the sources do not show a no-bailout principle.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Orbán says majority interests prevail and the government restricted the courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from the traditional family model and the government's anti-gender policies; the opened sources say nothing about parity quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The economy depends on exports and EU funds; autarky is not part of Orbanism.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from resistance to EU-imposed rules and the sovereignty emphasis.

moral-incentives.rationale: Work is morally valued in the work-based state, but material incentives such as tax cuts are the instrument.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Orbanism seeks power through elections; guerrilla vanguardism is foreign to it.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Fundamental Law honours the historical constitution but no hereditary titles are in play; neutral.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The National Avowal places Hungarian history and Christian Europe at the centre, and Orbán demands that nation be central in public life.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty emphasis and rejection of Western tutelage; no source on colonial paternalism.

patriotic-education.rationale: The National Avowal puts national pride and loyalty at the centre and the government sought a national curriculum; the sources show the ideal rather than curricula.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of race-conscious policy; no source addresses admissions.

public-money-creation.rationale: The government asserted control over the central bank, but no source on monetary reform; neutral.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Orbanism is a capitalist model with state direction and expects to manage crises; no direct statement.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Hungarian communities in the former kingdom's lands are the target of Article D, so cultivating influence there follows.

delink-world-market.rationale: Export-oriented and integrated through the EU; delinking has no role.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist thesis foreign to Orbanism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Article XV prohibits discrimination, yet Orbanism is not libertarian; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Boell and the Fundamental Law show majority-driven amendment and limits on constitutional courts, though a bill of rights exists.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the grievance over Trianon in the national framework of Article D; the sources do not say it directly.

elective-rulers.rationale: Not an Orbanist issue; the question is about throne succession, neutral.

minority-veto.rationale: Orbán says the majority is the foundation of democracy and individual freedoms cannot encroach on the community.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Boell describes weakened checks, but the ideology's own view on resistance is not addressed; neutral.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliament is formally supreme, but the Fundamental Law constrains it.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed in Orbanism sources; neutral.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed in Orbanism sources; neutral.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Boell describes a national middle class built from public funds, but the sources give no stance on duties of the wealthy; neutral.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Orbán says a national system values service to the nation and participation over private choices.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory question with no Orbanist view in the sources; neutral.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis with no Orbanist stance; neutral.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: Orbanism attacks Western elites but within an export, EU-funded model.

native-born-offices.rationale: Article D favours ethnic Hungarians; no source on native-born office reservation; neutral.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist question with no Orbanist counterpart; neutral.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from the work-based, self-sufficiency rhetoric and the sovereignty emphasis.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Article D and the status law show concern for kin abroad, but the sources describe non-territorial means, so adherents are split on demanding return.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from opposition to group-based claims; not discussed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Orbán's constitution emphasises Christian identity, not anti-fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from Orbanism's anti-communism and national-conservative identity; no source states this directly.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history topic with no Orbanist stance; neutral.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the national-conservative defence of heritage and anti-woke posture; no source on monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: No source gives an Orbanist stance; neutral.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: No source gives an Orbanist stance; neutral.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Orbán's 2014 speech holds Western liberal democracy failing and points to Singapore, China, Russia and Turkey as models for a Hungarian form.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Fundamental Law subordinates the army to the state; no guardian role in the sources.

paid-care-work.rationale: The pronatalist family policy supports mothers financially, but 'paid as labour' is not a stated doctrine.

filial-duty.rationale: Article XVI says adult children must care for parents in need.

office-by-exam.rationale: No source on civil-service recruitment methods; neutral.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The Orbanist economy uses nationalisation and sector taxes to favour national owners, so screening foreign takeovers fits it.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Article L protects marriage but the sources do not address divorce law; neutral.

recallable-delegates.rationale: A council-democracy idea alien to a party-led strong-state model.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The government nationalised private pension funds in 2010-11.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Article M and property protection are against communal tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Fundamental Law keeps a parliamentary budget; the governing majority passes it, so adherents accept the formal rule.

single-official-language.rationale: The National Avowal recognises nationalities in Hungary but the sources give no language policy; neutral.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the national-ownership economic policy; no direct statement in the sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from rejection of race-conscious liberal policy; not discussed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: No source gives a stance; neutral.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the sovereigntist non-interference stance; no direct source.

corporate-influence.rationale: Orbán attacks foreign and elite influence, but no stance on lobbying is sourced; neutral.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Orbanism treats foreign-financed civil society as political interference, and Hungary created a Sovereignty Protection Authority in 2024 to investigate foreign influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Article L encourages couples to have children and Orbán wants EU money directed to families having more children instead of migration.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the national-interest framing and Hungary's restrictions on land purchases by foreigners; local-resident quotas as such are not a stated position.

job-guarantee.rationale: The work-based state gives public work to the unemployed instead of welfare, which resembles a job offer of last resort, though adherents frame it as workfare rather than a right.

democratic-peace.rationale: Orbán rejects exporting liberal democracy and distrusts Western democracy-promotion; inferred from that stance, not from a statement on the democratic-peace thesis.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Fundamental Law stresses citizens' duties and the state's order, so adherents are unlikely to deny a duty to obey; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Orbán defends national sovereignty and rejects outside interference, from EU rule-of-law pressure to Western intervention, though no source states an absolute "for any reason" rule.

industrial-unions.rationale: Orbanism has no stated view on union structure; it is cool toward unions generally.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Adherents deny antisemitism and frame campaigns such as the anti-Soros one as about a network, not a minority; critics dispute this, so the answer is low confidence.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Fundamental Law protects marriage as the union of a man and a woman as the basis of the nation's survival.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Fundamental Law recognises access to data of public interest, but the government is widely criticised for restricting it, so adherents' stance is unclear.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from the economic-nationalist preference for domestic producers and food sovereignty; not a defining stance.

informal-organisation.rationale: Orbanism is built on a disciplined, permanent party and a strong state, the opposite of small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Orbán insists the Fundamental Law and national interest outrank EU and international bodies in matters of sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: The National Avowal credits Christianity with preserving the nation and Orbán calls the state Christian, though belonging is also defined by Hungarian descent and culture.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Orbanism stresses national sovereignty against Brussels and the liberal order; inferred from that, it does not accept ritual submission to a leading power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from a centralised, nation-first state that treats the Hungarian nation as one community; regional fiscal autonomy is not part of Orbanism.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Fundamental Law protects private property and the regime is anti-communist, so common ownership of productive property is rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Orbán draws on the anti-communist legacy of Fidesz, but pursues pragmatic ties with China and Russia, so this is inferred and not a stated doctrine.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Church and other independent providers run schools and social services, but the state has centralised and nationalised much of health and education; inferred as split.

religion-illusion.rationale: Orbanism defines Hungary as a Christian-national state and treats Christian culture as lasting, so it rejects the view that religion will fade.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from its pro-business, flat-tax, nationalist economy that values capitalism as a source of national wealth, though it is critical of multinational capital.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Orbanism opposes gender ideology and treats the family as the basis of the nation; inferred that it sees equality as achievable through family and law, not economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: The Fundamental Law makes the family the basis of the nation and Orbanist pronatalism supports family care, not public domestic services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language is part of its national-cultural stance, but no purge policy is documented; inferred as mild disagreement.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from its majority-over-minority-rights position that a government should keep freedom to alter such arrangements; the sources do not address it directly.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from a nation-state, family-centred, private-property model that rejects communal property.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from Orbanist nationalism, though it favours Hungarian communities abroad; no policy of settling the majority in minority regions is documented.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Orbán describes a work-based state that is neither liberal-capitalist nor socialist; inferred as a third-course claim.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Fundamental Law's National Avowal invokes Hungary's thousand-year statehood, and Orbán's government has made national and historical ties central, including support for ethnic Hungarians abroad; this is not a stated rule about competing claims, so medium.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Hungary's Fundamental Law and criminal code treat denial of the Holocaust as a crime, and the government rejects it officially, although it has been criticised over historical memory.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Hungary has not criminalised homosexuality since the 1960s and the government does not call for it, though it restricts LGBT rights through the Fundamental Law's definition of family; inferred as neutral.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Orbanism does not shut opposition parties, yet critics document pressure on media, courts, NGOs and universities; the 'illiberal' speech rejects independent checks while keeping elections, so adherents are split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Fundamental Law proclaims Christian heritage, but Hungary does not punish blasphemy or other faiths' practice; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Orbán's Hungary has no colonies and stresses national sovereignty; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed by the government's stated positions; it opposes migration but does not frame a religious duty. Inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The Fundamental Law and Orbán's speeches uphold electoral legitimacy and 'Christian liberties' rather than armed removal of rulers; inferred from the constitutional approach.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Orbán's 2014 'illiberal state' speech and the 2011 Fundamental Law favour a strong national community led by the state, while his governments use referendums and 'national consultations' sparingly as a plebiscitary device, not direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Orbán's speech holds that the national community outranks individual rights and rejects identity-based politics; the 2019 'Christian liberties' formulation defends the majority over group claims.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The Fundamental Law defines marriage as between a man and a woman and the 2020 amendment fixes sex as that at birth, and the government banned legal gender change; stated in the Fundamental Law.

assisted-dying.rationale: The Fundamental Law protects life from conception and Orbán's government emphasises Christian values; it has not legislated on assisted dying but the position follows from its principles.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Orbán has claimed his politics goes beyond left and right, combining national and social commitments; this is inferred from his speeches.

alienated-labor.rationale: Orbanism does not engage Marxist theory and favours work-based welfare, though it opposes global capital; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The government has framed Muslim migration as a threat to Christian Hungary and Europe, and Orbán has defended a Christian-national model of European identity.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The National Avowal opens 'God bless the Hungarians' and recognises Christianity's role; the Fundamental Law ties the state to Christian culture, although it does not claim authority comes from God rather than the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; the Fundamental Law is silent and the regime defends Christian symbols; inferred as split.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The government's labour policy has favoured employers, notably the 2018 overtime law, and does not prioritise this; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Orbán's work-based, interventionist and nationalist economy with sector taxes and national champions is neither laissez-faire nor a classic social market, and it has reduced welfare in favour of work-based support.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Hungary is a NATO member and Orbán defends national armed forces and border protection; the government has expanded its defence spending.

rich-first.rationale: Orbán's nationalist economics favours national elites ('national bourgeoisie') but he does not frame it this way; inferred as neutral.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Hungary is a member of NATO and the EU but Orbán has cultivated ties with Russia and China, describing an 'eastern opening'; adherents are split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: Hungary is a republic and Orban claims popular mandate, so hereditary office is foreign to the project.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: Orbanism favours Hungarian-owned banks and state direction rather than user-owned mutual banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Orbanism's 'unorthodox' economics and sovereignty politics reject conditions set by outside lenders such as the IMF.

property-franchise.rationale: The Fundamental Law and Orban's majoritarian democracy rest on universal suffrage; no wealth test is proposed.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: Orbanism defends traditional family roles and attacks 'gender ideology', so it rejects this feminist claim.

reification.rationale: Inferred: a Marxist-derived analysis at odds with its national, Christian framing of the economy.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: Orbanism treats liberal media as the problem and builds friendly media, not a class critique of press ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: the Fundamental Law states a rule-of-law order, although critics dispute practice.

racial-franchise.rationale: Hungary keeps universal suffrage under the Fundamental Law, and Orban frames the nation by culture and Christian identity, not a voting bar by race.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between direct 'national consultations' and a state-led model.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from critics' documented restrictions on public-information access and its majority-over-checks stance.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: Christian-national but the Fundamental Law defines marriage as man and woman without a faith bar.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: the government formally condemns antisemitism and such boycotts conflict with its stated Christian-national self-image.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: Orbanism prizes majority will expressed through elections and its own 'national consultations' over deliberative bodies chosen by lot; no source addresses assemblies directly.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: the Christian-national framing treats Christian tradition as a fixed civilisational anchor, not something to modernise; the sources do not discuss doctrinal reform.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Orbanism favours a nationally owned economy with concentrated domestic capital and does not treat wealth as a threat to liberty; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Orbanism defends a Christian-national conception of family and has restricted LGBT rights, so adherents would not endorse this; inferred, not a stated position on military service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Fundamental Law's National Avowal affirms Christianity's role in preserving the nation, and Orbanism is a Christian-national project, opposed to state atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Orbanism stresses order, security and a strong state, and treats policing and punishment as legitimate state duties.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Orbán holds that the majority's interests outrank other claims, which is the opposite of guaranteed communal shares; inferred for divided societies.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Orbanism favours churches and families over welfare dependence and funds church social services; the work-based alternative to welfare supports this, but state aid remains.

term-limits.rationale: Orbán has remained in office since 2010 and Orbanism emphasizes strong continuous leadership; no term-limit principle is stated, so this is inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Orbanism emphasizes majority rule via representative government and a strong executive, not delegated voting; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Orbanism prioritizes national and demographic concerns; extinction risk as a top policy priority is not stated, so inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Orbanism's Christian-conservative outlook leans traditional, but it does not address religious office, so this is inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Article L of the Fundamental Law protects marriage as a union of man and woman and Orbanism promotes traditional family roles; household authority is not addressed directly, so inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Orbanism ties political community to the Hungarian nation and citizenship (Fundamental Law, national avowal); extending even local votes to foreigners is not on its agenda and cuts against its community-first stance. Inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Orbanism favours market and family-owned property with a flat tax; Hungary capped rents only rarely and the sources do not show rent caps as a position. Inferred from its economic stance.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not discussed; Orbanism's national-capitalist economy and property-friendly Fundamental Law make abolishing IP unlikely. Inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Fidesz promotes patriotic education and the Fundamental Law stresses duties to the nation, but the sources document no drilled national-service youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Hungary has no nuclear weapons and the sources show no wish to host any; sovereignty-first rhetoric implies agreement, but this is not a stated position. Inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Orbán stresses national sovereignty and criticises Brussels, yet Hungary is a NATO member that hosts allied personnel; the sources are silent on bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Orbanism is split in practice: it commemorates the Trianon and Holocaust-era victims in national terms but disputes some historical framings (e.g. the 2014 occupation monument). Sources do not settle it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Orbán's work-based state and Fundamental Law (work as the basis of society, work-based alternative to welfare) hold that income should come from labour, though the flat tax and property protection temper it.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Orbanism's Christian-national, sovereigntist order accepts force for defence of the nation and borders; a pacifist ban on self-defence killing is not part of it. Inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Fundamental Law's National Avowal presents the Hungarian nation as continuous from St Stephen's founding of the state a thousand years ago, a core Orbanist national-historical claim.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Orbanism treats sex as a biological given: the Fundamental Law (Art. L) defines the father as male and mother as female, and the government has restricted gender-studies and legal gender change.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Orbanism does not do feminist politics; its family policy defines women by motherhood. The statement is about feminism's foundations, so the ideology has no direct stance; the answer is inferred as neutral.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The National Avowal honours those who fought for and died for the nation, but 'martyrs and saints' is religious language the sources do not attach to it. Inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Orbán frames politics as defence of Christian civilisation against liberal and migration pressures, but he mostly speaks in national-interest terms, not a cosmic good-versus-evil struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Orbanism treats Hungary as the centre of the Hungarian nation, including ethnic Hungarians abroad, who received citizenship in 2010 and are held to be one nation (Fundamental Law, Art. D); it does not seek to gather them all home.

culture-before-state.rationale: Orbán has pursued a cultural and 'culture war' agenda as the basis of national renewal alongside the state, but he built the state first in 2010; sources do not fix the order.

god-not-male.rationale: Orbán's Christian-national line uses traditional language and the Fundamental Law invokes God; the sources show no position on the gendering of God.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Orbanism treats traditional Christian family roles as the basis of the nation (Fundamental Law, Art. L), so it is unlikely to test scripture against a standard of women's full humanity. Inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Orbán explicitly seeks to give Hungarians (rather than foreign firms) ownership of key sectors such as banks, energy and retail, and the Fundamental Law and state policy reflect this economic nationalism.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Orbanism cares about Hungarian communities abroad but does not propose merging regions into ethnic territorial units; it mostly offers citizenship and support. Inferred.

missingStatements.text: Governments should be able to restrict foreign funding of NGOs, media and universities to protect national sovereignty.
missingStatements.rationale: Orbanism treats foreign-financed civil society as political interference, and Hungary created a Sovereignty Protection Authority in 2024 to investigate foreign influence.

missingStatements.text: The state should give families financial incentives to have more children, rather than rely on immigration to offset population decline.
missingStatements.rationale: Article L encourages couples to have children and Orbán wants EU money directed to families having more children instead of migration.

notes: Contested: whether Orbanism is a coherent ideology or a power-maximising method; answers on economy mix neoliberal elements (flat tax) with interventionism. Many answers on Marxist and distant topics are inferences.
